name: Yazid ibn al-Khadhdhaq
bio: Yazid ibn al-Khadhdhaq belonged to the Shann division of 'Abd al-Qais, on the north-western shore of the Persian Gulf. Lyall notes that Ode LXXVIII is sometimes ascribed to his brother Suwaid.
Both of his pieces defy an-Nu'man Abu Qabus (circa A.D. 582-605), who tried to levy taxation from the tribe.

poems.title: Ode LXXVIII: I have made ready Sabhah for
poems.author: Yazid ibn al-Khadhdhaq
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Yazid son of al-Khadhdhaq, of Shann, of 'Abd al-Qais.
poems.text:
I have made ready Sabhah for action, now that she has attained her sixth year, and I have clad myself in the armament of a man of good judgement who endures hardship patiently.

Ye cannot join together love of me and anger with me— unless two swords can be brought together in one sheath.

Nu'man ! verily thou art a traitor and a cheat : thy inward mind hides a purpose other than that which thou showest forth.

And if thou thinkest of stripping the bark off our tamarisk-tree, try it, then, if thou art obstinate in thy purpose !

That we are proud, and draw our origin from a glorious stock, forbids us [to abase ourselves before thee].

If thou in thy folly attackest our kinsmen, thou shalt find squadrons of horsemen galloping to defend us.

Didst thou fancy that we were flesh set forth on a board, or think that we should not defend ourselves in time of trouble ?

Thou didst practise deceit, trampling on our faces ; and the deceit in thee was a sign of thy purpose ;

And thou didst brandish thy sword as though thou wouldst bring war upon us. Look to thy sword ! whom dost thou mean to slay with it ?

Thou tookest in hand a task suited only to a prudent warrior, whilst thou wast distraught, a man destroyed by what he plotted ;

And now in sooth the way is light before thee, and the paths for thee to tread are manifest, and guidance helps thee on.

poems.title: Ode LXXIX: Have the tidings not reached her
poems.author: Yazid ibn al-Khadhdhaq
poems.text:
Have the tidings not reached her that I have ready the armament of a man of good judgement, and that I have already trained ash-Shamus for war ?

I gave her the training-food, so that in the course of the winter her colour grew darker, as though there were upon her a veil of brocade and a sombre-hued hood ;

We set apart for her support during the summer our milch-camels, those in the seventh year of age, and those of the ninth and eighth year.

And she became finally like the wild-goat fed on the herbage that does not fail in drought ; she springs, when she gallops, on nimble legs that rise high in air, having a large reserve of speed.

We keep ready for the day of alarm a smooth coat of mail, ample, polished and shining, and a keen-edged sword, light and quick in its stroke, evil-natured [to its foes].

[We carry upon her our arms nobly in every fight, when the closely-serried host stands face to face with the [enemy's] line.]

Guard thine oath with a reserve — mayst thou be saved from cursing ! — the word of a sinful man, [which thou didst swear] against our goods, that they should surely be divided [as booty] into fifths !

Whensoever we have traversed one sandy tract and its border, we have an affair in another, quick to put through, into which we plunge.

Turn away from us, ye Sons of an-Nu'man, your breasts: if ye do not so, ye will have to turn away your heads against your will.

Shall every mean man among you, every base-born wretch, count up against us a raid and spoiling ?

Dost thou think and imagine us to be like the Son of al-Mu'alla, sea-faring men, that we should pay dues to the tax-gatherers ?

If ye will send a spy to search us out, he will find around my tents the whole tribe sitting.
